newsitem.title: USA: Cali trafficker names Mexican ex-officials - report.
newsitem.headline: Cali trafficker names Mexican ex-officials - report.

text.p: An imprisoned Cali drug cartel kingpin identified senior officials under former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari as having been bought off by Mexican drug cartels, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
The Miami Herald said sworn testimony from Juan Carlos Ramirez Abadia marked the first time a major Colombian trafficker had implicated senior Mexican officials in narcotics smuggling.

Ramirez, in sworn testimony to Mexican prosecutors on April 7 and 8, said cocaine shipments through Mexico were protected by Mexico's former Deputy Attorney General, Javier Coello Trejo, and Guillermo Gonzalez Calderoni, former Judicial Police Commander, the Herald reported.

"Coello Trejo ... permitted the activities of the cartels, and they paid him for this," the newspaper said Ramirez told the Mexican prosecutors, citing information from "parts of the 12-page sworn testimony read to The Herald."
Gonzalez Calderoni and a federal police commander in Tijuana, Guillermo "Memo" Salazar, made sure police and soldiers did not interfere with cocaine shipments, Ramirez said.
"The airstrips were protected by the federal police and the huachos," Ramirez said, using the slang word for soldiers.
The Tijuana commander charged traffickers $800 to $1,000 for each kilo of cocaine delivered in the United States, Ramirez said.

The allegations are the latest in a series of charges against Coello Trejo and Gonzalez Calderoni, who left their posts amid accusations by the Mexican government that they had ties to drug traffickers. Both have denied the allegations.

In October, a former Mexican police commander who joined the Gulf Cartel testified at the Houston, Texas, trial of drug cartel chieftain Juan Garcia Abrego that bribes totalling $1.5 million a month were paid to Coello Trejo and two other officials for protection.

Ramirez turned himself in to Colombian authorities in March 1996, following the lead of other Cali cartel chiefs. He was convicted of drug trafficking in Cali last November and sentenced to more than 13 years in prison.
He gave the testimony to Mexican prosecutors in an apparent bid to have his sentence shortened, the Herald said.
